notes: §1985:XII.2.4 GR12 (the 1993 amendment): "The text produced as a result of the complete processing of a COPY statement must not contain a COPY statement." ResolveOneCopy asks FindStatementKeyword whether the library text holds a COPY statement and, below 2002, refuses it at the outer COPY through the constructs row copy-nested-library-text-2002 (COBOL0900); the other way the produced text can hold one, a REPLACING operand that introduces COPY, is ApplyReplacements' ForbiddenIn (COBOL2574, every edition). Probes at --std 85: the witness (PB5126OU holds COPY PB5126IN) refused, and also with REPLACING on the outer COPY; REPLACING ==DISPLAY XX.== BY ==COPY LIBLIT.== and a pseudo-text-2 ending in COPY LIBLIT refused (COBOL2451 + COBOL2574); library text with COPY only inside an alphanumeric literal and on a comment line ran (prints COPY LIBX.); a copied AUTHOR comment-entry holding the word COPY ran (SR10); the witness at --std 2002 runs START OUTER INNER END.

next.reason: 1985 (1993 amendment): 'The text produced as a result of the complete processing of a COPY statement must not contain a COPY statement', so no copied text may hold a COPY. 2023 is looser. §2023:7.2.3.3 SR1 allows a COPY statement 'in source text or in library text'. §2023:7.2.3.4 GR12 says 'If the REPLACING phrase is not specified, the library text may contain a COPY statement that does not include a REPLACING phrase', and requires support for at least 5 nesting levels. The bar remains only where §2023:7.2.3.4 GR10 applies ('If the REPLACING phrase is specified, the library text shall not contain a COPY statement') and where §2023:7.2.3.4 GR13 applies ('The replacing action of a COPY statement shall not introduce a COPY statement'). A program 1985 must refuse, nested COPY without REPLACING, is legal in 2023. Both editions check this at compile time; no exception condition is involved.
